rv.q: Lieberman has fashioned an evening that is untidy, ambitious, funny, and unexpectedly tender.
Leaning more toward this kind of actual history and away from the story of the two couples would have given “Dirty Books” more of the heft that the subject deserves, because this is not just history.
It’s also, unfortunately, a bit of a snooze.
The moment was one of many that felt like a shared experience had united us all.
It’s a dynamic celebration of the vastness of what it can mean to share a life with someone and what it means to do so unapologetically.
It all felt shoehorned together, but by the end I came to mostly appreciate it.

cn.t: This immersive dive into book banning and anti-obscenity laws draws mixed reviews. Critics praise its playful creativity and historical context, but some find the execution bland despite the provocative subject matter.

vr.q: I did genuinely appreciate the dramaturgical ambition to it. And more than that, I was just fascinated by this whole experience.
